meta.title: Yishuv · A Chassidishe Moshav in Binyamin
meta.description: A heimishe Chassidishe moshav in the hills of Binyamin, half an hour from Yerushalayim — built by American families, for American families. Now forming the founding garin.

hero.pasuk_en: “For Your servants cherish her stones, and love her very dust.”
hero.title: A heimishe Chassidishe moshav in Eretz Yisroel for American families
hero.subtitle: In the hills of Binyamin, half an hour from Yerushalayim. Private homes, gardens and open space — and a kehilla of our own.

history.title: In every generation
history.lede: Yidden have always yearned and striven to go up and live in Eretz Yisroel — our home.

items.text: **The Ramban** arrives in Yerushalayim and rebuilds its Jewish community.
**The Shelah HaKadosh** leaves Prague to settle in Eretz Yisroel.
**The Ohr HaChaim** reaches Yerushalayim with his talmidim.
**The Baal Shem Tov** sets out with true mesirus nefesh — but is not zoche to arrive.
**Talmidei HaBaal Shem Tov** — some 300 Chassidim — go up together as a chaburah, led by R’ Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk.
**Talmidei HaGra** follow — and aliyah never stops, to this very day.
A true kibbutz galuyos: over **4,300** olim from France, **3,300** from America, nearly **1,000** from England.

challenges.title: So many of us long to live here — and to stay.
challenges.lede: Why staying is so hard, and how the moshav answers each challenge.

items.title: Kehilla
items.problem: No established kehilla of American Chassidish families. Far from parents and family, a kehilla is everything — without one, most who came “for a few years” go back.
items.answer: A kehilla built by American Chassidish families, for American Chassidish families.

items.title: Housing
items.problem: Yerushalayim rents are steep, and buying a home is nearly impossible.
items.answer: Land for a symbolic sum — and a real path to owning your own home.

items.title: Space & calm
items.problem: Tiny apartments and crowded, noisy streets — no room to raise children with menuchas hanefesh.
items.answer: Private homes, gardens, and open space.

items.title: Chinuch
items.problem: Few mosdos are both serious Chassidish and right for American children — with Yiddish, English and Hebrew all in the mix.
items.answer: Mosdos for our community, with Hebrew–English integration from day one.

items.title: Parnassah
items.problem: Careers don’t transfer easily — and when support from home runs out, so does the plan to stay.
items.answer: Work near home: remote-work infrastructure, local businesses, and a local economy over time.

items.title: Putting down roots
items.problem: Renting, moving, waiting — everything about how we live here says “for now.”
items.answer: Ownership from the start: a caravilla that’s yours in 2½ years, then a permanent home.

process.title: Three stages, from garin to town

stages.label: Stage A
stages.title: Forming the garin
stages.lede: First we build the group. The land comes after.

cards.title: The founders
cards.text: 50+ families ready to be the founders, making the decisions together.

cards.title: Proof of demand
cards.text: Until now, new yishuvim have been built almost only by the dati-leumi community. A large, serious group shows the authorities real demand from ours.

cards.title: The land
cards.text: Open land in Binyamin, ½ hour from Yerushalayim — or, with a serious group, one of two already-approved yishuvim off Route 443, between Givat Ze’ev and Modi’in.

stages.note: Working with the Mateh Binyamin Regional Council — not an outpost.

stages.label: Stage B
stages.title: Moving in
stages.intro: New yishuvim usually start with Amana’s basic rental caravans: ₪1,000–3,000 a month depending on size (about ₪1,000 per 45 m²), plus ₪1,000 for infrastructure. They’re simple, budget units — not right for every family. **So we’re offering two better options:**

cards.title: Buy a caravilla
cards.text: A high-standard caravilla, finished inside like a beautiful home. **0% financing over 30 monthly payments** — roughly what you’d pay in rent in Yerushalayim. After 2½ years it’s fully paid off, and it’s yours.

cards.title: Rent a caravilla
cards.text: The same high-standard caravilla, rented from Amana for a much lower monthly cost. We’re working to convince Amana to offer it.
A real town: streets, infrastructure, every communal need.
Land through bar-reshut or a ~50-year lease for a symbolic sum — you pay mainly for infrastructure.
Infrastructure per 500 m² plot — rough estimate (about $65,000).

numbers.title: The founders’ advantage

advantages.title: The land
advantages.text: Land comes through bar-reshut or a ~50-year lease for only a symbolic sum — founders pay mainly for infrastructure.

advantages.title: A real say
advantages.text: This is not a developer. Every family who is there has an equal say in how the moshav is set up.

numbers.later_sub: rough estimate, based on the yishuv Adam
numbers.compare_note: Bars drawn to scale. Rough estimates — about one-tenth the price for founders already there when zoning comes through.
numbers.allin_title: A spacious ~300 m² home on its own plot.
numbers.allin_text: Rough estimate: land through bar-reshut, infrastructure as above, and regular building costs for a ~300 m² house.

vision.title: Imagine what we can build —
vision.text: As founders, we’re not buying into someone else’s plan. Together, we decide what this community becomes.

ideas.title: Kehilla & Parnassah

vision.voice_title: Every founding family has a voice.
vision.voice_text: Together we choose what to build, what comes first, and how it’s funded. These are ideas, not promises — each one is built only if the founders choose it and it’s viable.
